observations: Photo 0 shows a black Nikon D3300 DSLR body with a body cap on the mount.
An 18-55mm VR II lens sits next to the camera on the box.
The box reads "Nikon D3300 18-55 VR II Kit" and "AF-S DX NIKKOR 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G VR II".
"Nikon D3300" is printed on the camera front and top right.
Lens barrel shows "Nikon", "AF-S DX NIKKOR 18-55mm 1:3.5-5.6G VR II", and focal length marks.
Both photos are taken in what appears to be a camera shop with boxed accessories in the background.

identity.model: D3300 with AF-S DX NIKKOR 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G VR II lens

claims.evidence: Not visible in photos; model identification supports it but image does not prove sensor specs.

claims.claim: Like new, never repaired or opened
claims.evidence: Cannot be confirmed from photos alone.
No power-on or function test shown in photos.
Receipt and warranty not shown in photos.

risks.risk: Camera body may not power on or may have shutter/sensor faults.
risks.proof: Video of camera turning on, navigating menus, and taking a test photo.

risks.risk: Lens autofocus, VR, zoom, or aperture may be faulty.
risks.proof: Video of lens zooming, focusing, and VR engaging when attached to camera.

risks.risk: Body may have been opened or repaired despite claim.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of screw seals and battery compartment interior.

risks.risk: Receipt or warranty may be missing or invalid.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the original receipt and warranty card.
risks.if_unproven: as no warranty or proof of purchase

risks.risk: Sensor or mirror box may have mold, dust, or scratches.
risks.proof: Photo of mirror box and sensor area illuminated.
risks.if_unproven: as sensor or mirror box damaged

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on, navigating menus, and taking a photo.
Video of the lens zooming, focusing, and VR working when attached.
Close-up photos of the original receipt and warranty card.
Close-up photo of the camera mirror box and sensor area.
response.reason: The camera and lens are identifiable by brand and model from the photos, so a worst-case price can be set even though the seller's condition claims are unproven.
